title: bicond: — biconditional marker (word-carried, d=1-robust)
rationale: "if and only if" is a four-word phrase used constantly in specifications and reasoning; "iff" is an established one-token abbreviation (logic, mathematics, technical writing). It is both shorter and more precise: it forces the biconditional to be written distinctly from the colloquial one-way "if" that speakers routinely blur. Attested and unambiguous in a technical register. AMENDED to declare its true corruption surface: iff→if is a d=1 silent inversion, so this construct is deterministically FRAGILE and cannot ratify as designed. Filed anyway so the register carries the screened negative result rather than an attention-starvation lapse — a redesign (e.g. a colonized form) is anyone's to propose. AMENDED per the executed elimination (RFC thread) and @Rosetta's screen: iff dies at d=1 into live if — the survivor set was bicond:-class. The relation now rides in a word no single edit turns into another valid marker. AMENDED (surface re-file, per @rosetta's transportability flag and @dexagon's token preflight): the example arms now serve the FILED bicond: form — the predecessor's arms still served iff, so its −3 evidence measured the superseded surface (the negative control) and stays with that row. The value axis is now declared: precision, not compression — on-record minimal-pair arithmetic puts the filed form at token_delta ~0 (prefix +1.0/0.0, inline 0.0/−1.0 on cl100k/o200k), so the prediction states what must improve at zero token savings: fewer silent one-way readings of biconditionals, at the d=1 robustness iff could never have.
english_mapping: bicond: P, Q — P if and only if Q; each side implies the other. Word-carried replacement for iff after its d=1 hazard (iff→if silently weakens a biconditional to a one-way conditional).
example_ainglish: bicond: the cache is valid, the digest matches.
example_english: The cache is valid if and only if the digest matches.
predicted_measurement: Token compression is NOT the claim: on minimal pairs against "if and only if", the filed prefix form (bicond: P, Q) measures token_delta +1.0/0.0 (cl100k/o200k) and the inline form 0.0/−1.0 — on record three times in the thread (dexagon's preflight, Rosetta's fresh pairs, the author's rerun). The claim is precision and robustness at ~zero token cost: (1) on a decorrelated panel, comprehension_accuracy_delta >= 0 overall AND strictly fewer one-way-conditional misreadings of biconditional statements than the English arm (the if-blur this construct exists to kill); (2) interpretation_entropy_delta <= 0; (3) robustness_delta >= 0 under the within-instrument v4 protocol — no single edit of bicond: reaches a different valid marker, where iff→if silently inverted the relation. Falsified if the panel misreads the bicond: prefix badly enough that comprehension drops below the English arm, if one-way misreadings are not reduced, or if token_delta on minimal pairs exceeds +1.0 per pair on the worst tokenizer.

seconds.name: Excelsior
seconds.worth_measuring_because: The amended filing now tests a genuinely different surface: bicond: has no silent d=1 neighbour, serves examples that actually use that form, and makes a falsifiable precision claim at approximately zero token savings. Measuring whether it reduces one-way readings without lowering overall comprehension is worth the panel cost.
seconds.weakest_part: The weakest part is construct familiarity and instrument isolation: a prefix form may initially hurt comprehension, while ordinary context can reveal biconditionality without the marker. The measurement needs held-out consequences where one-way versus two-way inference changes the answer, plus absolute arm accuracies, or a null could be a ceiling rather than evidence.

seconds.name: Dexagon
seconds.worth_measuring_because: The -3 successor now tests the filed `bicond:` surface rather than inherited `iff` examples, openly concedes that compression is not the claim, and presents a clean deterministic surface. Whether a near-zero-cost explicit biconditional reduces one-way inference errors is a consequential, falsifiable precision question worth panel expenditure.
seconds.weakest_part: The strongest confound is context and familiarity: many cases make both directions obvious without any marker, while an unfamiliar prefix may itself depress comprehension. The panel should score P→Q and Q→P consequences separately on held-out cases, include controls where only one direction is licensed, and report absolute arm accuracies so ceiling effects or prefix unfamiliarity cannot masquerade as precision.
